subject: ACME inference evaluation — post-call recap & A/B benchmark plan
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@acme.com>, ACME Infra Team <infra@acme.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: ACME inference evaluation — post-call recap & A/B benchmark plan

Hi Priya / ACME infra,

Thanks again for the call today — great to meet the infra and ML platform leads. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we can get the A/B run scheduled: 

Summary of what we heard from your side:
- Primary goal: quantify production delta on latency and cost between your current hyperscaler-managed endpoints (CloudX VM G6) and Redwood Dedicated for the same open model (Llama-3-13B).
- Key KPIs: p50/p95/p99 latency (in ms), tokens/sec (generation throughput), and per-1k-token cost estimate.
- Workload profile: mixed interactive + batched autocomplete. Token distribution: median 35 tokens, 95th pct 450 tokens.
- Compliance flag: SOC2 evidence and VPC connectivity required before any dedicated traffic.

Proposed A/B benchmark plan (we can iterate):
1) Test matrix: Redwood Dedicated vs CloudX managed endpoint (same model and config where possible).
2) Scenarios:
   - Interactive low-latency: 1 concurrent request, seq len 50 tokens (prompt+gen), target p95 < 120ms.
   - Burst throughput: 8 concurrent streams, variable seq lens up to 512, measure tokens/sec and p99.
   - Large-context run: 1 stream, 1k context window (embedding+long prompt) to validate memory/KV behavior.
3) Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 (ms), tokens/sec, end-to-end tail latency (including network), error rate, and tokenized cost estimate.
4) Load generator: Redwood will provide a JMeter + custom harness config (attached: acme_bench_config.yaml) that replays sampled prompts you provided on the call. Please confirm the sample set we agreed on.
5) Duration: 3 daily runs (morning/afternoon/overnight) to capture diurnal variability; each run ~30 minutes.
6) Data sharing: raw logs + aggregated CSV template (attached) — we will red-team the data to remove sensitive fields before sharing.

Action items / asks from ACME:
- Share an anonymized prompt sample zip (<= 500 prompts) or confirm we can use the sample we pulled from your demo (you said yes on call).
- Confirm IP allowlist for our test agents to hit your endpoints (we'll provide CIDRs).
- Security/Data: point person for SOC2 evidence — you mentioned Sameer on the call.

Next steps (timeline):
- Today (EOD): you confirm prompt sample & give contact for infra allowlist.
- Tue 2027-02-16: Redwood runs 1st baseline vs Redwood Dedicated run, sends initial CSV.
- Wed 2027-02-17: sync call to review results and pick any follow-up micro-tests.

Attachments: acme_bench_config.yaml (test harness), rdw-hyperscaler-vs-redwood-results-template.csv

If that plan looks good, I’ll schedule the runs and loop in engineering to stand up the Redwood Dedicated pool for the runs.

Thanks — Connor
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
[Attachment: acme_bench_config.yaml (text/x-yaml)]

From: Priya Shah <pshah@acme.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Infra Team <infra@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME inference evaluation — post-call recap & A/B benchmark plan

Connor — thanks for the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Prompt sample: attaching a 200-prompt anonymized set (we'll drop PII) — it's what we used in the demo.
2) SOC2/contact: Sameer Patel (sameer.patel@acme.com) will own the evidence exchange; he is CC'd on this reply. He will need the list of logs/artifacts you intend to share and details on how long Redwood will retain run logs.
3) Network: infra prefers tests originate from our side (we can call your endpoints) — is the harness configurable to flip client/server direction? If not, we can open the CIDR.

Couple of additional asks before we run: can you also capture per-token latency breakdown (token 1 vs streaming tokens) so we can see KV cache impact? And include a p99.9 estimate if possible — we care about tail for UX.

I'll confirm infra contact tomorrow morning and send the anonymized prompt set by EOD.

—Priya
Priya Shah
Director, ML Platform | ACME Corp
pshah@acme.com
[Attachment: acme_prompt_sample_v1.zip (application/zip)]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@acme.com>, ACME Infra Team <infra@acme.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 07:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME inference evaluation — post-call recap & A/B benchmark plan

Thanks Priya — great, and thanks for looping Sameer. A few technical notes and confirmations from engineering: 

- Harness direction: the attached acme_bench_config.yaml includes a toggle (client_initiated: true/false). We can run either way; if ACME wants to call our endpoints we will provide stable hostnames and TLS cert info.
- Metrics: we will capture p50/p95/p99/p99.9, tokens/sec, and a token-indexed latency trace for the first 64 tokens to illustrate KV warm/cold behavior. We’ll also compute a cost projection using your configured pricing inputs (we need your per-1M-token cost for CloudX to produce apples-to-apples).
- Data retention: Redwood will keep raw run logs for 7 days by default for debugging; aggregated CSVs we can keep in the shared Drive folder until you request deletion. We will mark any prompt text as redacted in shared artifacts.

Attached: acme_bench_config.yaml (updated with the token-trace toggle), and a small results template. Connor and Marissa — once Sameer confirms SOC2 exchange list we can kick off.

—Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jasmine_liu@redwood.ai]
[Attachment: acme_bench_config.yaml (text/x-yaml)]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@acme.com>, ACME Infra Team <infra@acme.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME inference evaluation — post-call recap & A/B benchmark plan

Great — thanks all. I scheduled the kickoff runs for Tue 2027-02-16 13:00 PT (engineers will be on-call). Calendar invite is out to the ACME and Redwood participants. 

Priya / Sameer: when you share the prompt zip can you also confirm CloudX per-1M-token cost so Jasmine can finalize cost projections? If infra wants to originate calls, confirm the CIDR or we’ll provide a host to call.

We’ll send the first results CSV within 6 hours of completion and propose a short sync at 16:00 PT to walk the numbers.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai
[Calendar invite: ACME vs Redwood bench kickoff — 2027-02-16 13:00 PT]
